correctness.rationale: The entire transform is reconstructed from two lexicographically sorted suffix populations; its four exceptional BWT positions and all tie rules are proved. A nonnegative run-count defect identity yields the upper bound, equality families, exact extremizer series and two-point law. A distinct suffix argument proves the reversal denominator bound. Finite checks compare 4096 complete literal BWT strings with the normal form and verify fixed-length counts 4–28, but are not substituted for infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The closest inspected papers study cyclic BWT reversal asymmetry for standard/Fibonacci families, construction of the general sentinel run-length BWT, or sentinel placement in BWT output words. They do not state the full forward four-run transform, optimizer partition, extremizer generating function, or conditional two-point limit. The scope difference and absence of direct implication are made explicit; unindexed equivalent specializations remain a risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent four-run special case may occur in unindexed or inaccessible literature.
General BWT facts are classical, so originality is claimed only for the joint exact symbolic formula, sharp classification and conditional distribution, not for the ability to compute a BWT.

value.rationale: The BWT run count controls the size of compressed suffix indexes. The four-run family is the first binary alternating-run family with two separate zeros and two separate ones. A complete normal form and optimizer classification expose how four source runs create up to nine transform runs. The generating function counts all optimal inputs, the nondegenerate two-point limit describes typical inputs, and the 9/4 reversal witness connects to the 2020 reversal-asymmetry question. The result is a natural full classification, not a finite arbitrary table.
